lessons.title: Newborn Physical Examination & Common Findings

content_chunks.visual_description: Memorize these ranges - they're tested constantly!
details: **Heart Rate**: 120-160 bpm (can go 100 sleeping, 180 crying)
**Respiratory Rate**: 30-60 breaths/min (periodic breathing normal - pauses <20 sec)
**Blood Pressure**: ~70/45 mmHg (systolic increases ~1 mmHg per day first week)
**Temperature**: 97.7-99.5°F (36.5-37.5°C) axillary
**Weight**: 2,500-4,000g (5.5-8.8 lbs). Lose up to 10% first 3-5 days, regain by 2 weeks.
**Length**: 48-53 cm (19-21 inches)
**Head Circumference (OFC)**: 33-37 cm (average 34-35cm). Should be 2-3cm larger than chest.
**Chest Circumference**: 30-33 cm

content_chunks.visual_description: Picture the baby's journey through the birth canal - head gets squeezed!
details: **Cranial Molding**: Overlapping skull bones creating temporary 'cone head'. Resolves in days. NORMAL!
**Caput Succedaneum**: Scalp edema/swelling that CROSSES suture lines. Soft, puffy. Resolves 24-48 hours. NORMAL!
**Cephalohematoma**: Blood collection UNDER periosteum, does NOT cross suture lines. Firm edges. Takes weeks to resolve. Risk: jaundice from RBC breakdown. Usually benign.
**Subgaleal Hemorrhage**: EMERGENCY! Blood under scalp, CROSSES suture lines, enlarging head circumference, signs of hypovolemia. Rare but life-threatening. Requires NICU admission.
**Fontanelles**: Anterior (diamond, 1-4cm, closes 9-18mo), Posterior (triangle, <1cm, closes 1-2mo). Sunken = dehydration. Bulging = increased ICP.
content_chunks.mnemonic: **'Caput CROSSES suture lines, Cephalohematoma does NOT'** (like their first letters: C-C, C-N)

content_chunks.concept: Skin Findings: The Rainbow of Newborn Rashes
content_chunks.visual_description: Imagine a newborn with a patchwork of colors and textures - most are benign!
details: **Milia**: Tiny white papules on nose/chin (blocked sebaceous glands). Resolve spontaneously. NORMAL!
**Erythema Toxicum**: 'Flea-bitten' rash - erythematous macules/papules with central white/yellow pustule. Appears day 1-3, lasts <1 week. Benign. Contains eosinophils (not infection!).
**Acrocyanosis**: Blue hands/feet while body pink. Due to immature circulation. NORMAL first 24-48 hours.
**Central Cyanosis**: Blue lips/tongue/trunk. ABNORMAL! Indicates hypoxia - needs immediate evaluation for heart/lung disease.
**Transient Neonatal Pustular Melanosis**: Brown macules with collarette of scale, pustules. Present at birth, more common in Black infants. Benign, resolves 1-2 months.
**Jaundice**: Yellow skin/sclera. PATHOLOGIC if <24 hours old, rapidly rising bilirubin, or conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Check bilirubin level!
**Mongolian Spots**: Blue-gray patches on sacrum/buttocks. More common in darker-skinned babies. Benign, fade over years. DOCUMENT to prevent abuse concerns later!
content_chunks.clinical_pearl: 🚨 **Jaundice in first 24 hours = PATHOLOGIC until proven otherwise!** Always check bilirubin. Likely hemolysis (ABO/Rh incompatibility, G6PD deficiency).

content_chunks.visual_description: Differentiate the 'stork bites' (benign) from port-wine stains (need evaluation)
details: **Nevus Simplex ('Stork Bite', 'Angel Kiss')**: Flat pink patches on nape of neck, eyelids, glabella. MOST COMMON birthmark (70-80%). Fade over months-years. Benign.

**Port-Wine Stain (Nevus Flammeus)**: Dark red-purple, flat, sharply demarcated, does NOT blanch, does NOT fade. If involves V1 trigeminal distribution (forehead/eye) → Sturge-Weber syndrome risk (get MRI, ophthalmology eval).

**Cavernous Hemangioma (Infantile Hemangioma)**: Raised, bright red 'strawberry' lesion. Not present at birth (appears weeks 1-4). Grows rapidly first 6-12 months, then involutes over years. Problematic if near eye, nose, mouth (can interfere with function) → refer to dermatology for propranolol treatment.
content_chunks.clinical_pearl: ⚠️ **Port-wine stain in V1 distribution = Sturge-Weber until proven otherwise!** Risk of seizures, glaucoma, developmental delay. Needs neuroimaging and ophthalmology.

content_chunks.visual_description: Listen carefully - distinguishing innocent from pathologic murmurs saves lives
details: **Physiologic Split S2**: Heard at upper left sternal border, increases with inspiration. NORMAL!
**Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)**: Continuous 'machine-like' murmur, bounding pulses. Usually closes by 2-3 days in term infants. Persists in preemies.
**Critical Congenital Heart Disease (CCHD) Screening**: Pulse oximetry on right hand AND one foot before discharge. PASS if both ≥95% AND difference <3%. FAIL = echocardiogram.
**Cyanosis with feeding/crying**: Think cyanotic heart disease (Tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of great vessels). Needs urgent cardiology.
**Femoral pulses**: MUST palpate! Diminished/absent = coarctation of aorta (upper extremity BP > lower extremity BP).
content_chunks.clinical_pearl: 🫀 **No murmur doesn't rule out critical heart disease!** Many cyanotic lesions are ductal-dependent and present when ductus closes (day 2-7). This is why pulse ox screening is mandated.

details: **Hypospadias**: Urethral opening on ventral surface of penis (underside). NEVER circumcise - foreskin needed for surgical repair!
**Hydrocele**: Transilluminating scrotal swelling. Communicating (fluctuates) vs. non-communicating. Most resolve by 1 year. Surgery if persists after age 1.
**Undescended Testicle (Cryptorchidism)**: Testicle not in scrotum. Re-examine at every visit. If not descended by 6 months, refer to urology (orchiopexy by 12-18 months to preserve fertility).
**Hymenal Tag**: Small tissue projection from hymen in girls. Benign, resolves spontaneously.
**Labial Adhesions**: Fusion of labia minora in girls (more common in infancy/toddlerhood). Usually asymptomatic. Treat with estrogen cream if interfering with urination.

content_chunks.visual_description: Feel for the 'clunk' of a dislocatable hip - early detection prevents disability
details: **Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (DDH)**: Hip instability/dislocation. Higher risk: breech, female, family history, firstborn.
**Barlow Maneuver**: Adduct hip while pushing posteriorly - dislocatable hip 'clunks' OUT of socket.
**Ortolani Maneuver**: Abduct hip while pulling anteriorly - dislocated hip 'clunks' back INTO socket.
**Asymmetric skin folds**: Unequal thigh creases suggest hip dislocation.
**Galeazzi Sign**: Unequal knee heights when hips/knees flexed - positive in DDH.
**If positive exam or risk factors**: Hip ultrasound <6 months old OR X-ray if >6 months. Refer to orthopedics for Pavlik harness.
content_chunks.mnemonic: **'Barlow = Bad, pushes OUT. Ortolani = OK, puts back IN'**

story_intro.text: You're handed a fresh 24-hour-old newborn for the first well-baby check. Parents anxiously hover: 'Is everything normal?' As you unwrap the blanket, you see blue hands, a pointy head, white dots on the nose, and a stork-bite mark on the forehead. Let's distinguish normal newborn variants from true pathology.
story_intro.visual_cue: 👶 Picture a vernix-covered newborn with milia, a cephalohematoma that doesn't cross suture lines, and acrocyanosis of hands/feet while body is pink.

clinical_pearls: **APGAR Score**: Done at 1 and 5 minutes. Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration (0-2 each). 7-10 = normal. <7 at 5 min = increased risk neurologic issues.
**First Void & Stool**: Should void within 24 hours, stool (meconium) within 48 hours. If not, consider GI obstruction (Hirschsprung, imperforate anus) or renal agenesis.
**Umbilical Cord Care**: Keep dry, fold diaper down. Cord falls off 1-3 weeks. Oozing/redness/odor = omphalitis (EMERGENCY - can lead to sepsis).
**Red Light Reflex**: Check both eyes. Absent or white reflex = retinoblastoma, congenital cataract, retinopathy of prematurity. REFER immediately to ophthalmology.
**Tongue-Tie (Ankyloglossia)**: Short lingual frenulum limiting tongue movement. If interfering with breastfeeding, refer to ENT for frenotomy.
